claims.claim: Reachability is exactly a sparse unary congruence-closure query.
claims.evidence: Let R relate wires connected by a legal stack-neutral path above the bottom marker. Reversibility and concatenation make R an equivalence. If same-box edges (o,X,t) and (o',X,t') have t R t', pushing along the first edge, lifting the neutral path to the enlarged stack, and popping along the reverse second edge proves o R o'; hence leastness gives θ⊆R. Conversely, every bottom-neutral word has a well-nested decomposition into concatenations and push-X/balanced/pop-X excursions. Structural induction applies the folding rule to each excursion and proves R⊆θ. The accepting transition is available exactly at an outer-pin wire with bottom symbol exposed, establishing the exit query. Stability also makes [t]↦[o] a well-defined partial unary operation for each X.
claims.witness: A generating fold is realized concretely as o|S → t|XS, followed by a neutral path t|XS → t'|XS, followed by t'|XS → o'|S.
claims.search_method: Direct two-inclusion proof reconstructed from the source DPDA transitions and the least folding equivalence.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic O(B+(W+E) log(W+E))-time, O(W+E+B)-space algorithm, eliminating the dense W·B initialization.
claims.evidence: Each retained map entry represents one box among edges entering a current target class. A collision has already-equivalent targets, so its queued origin merge is forced by θ. Deleted entries remain represented transitively by the retained origin after pending merges finish. At quiescence, every pair of original same-box edges with equivalent targets has equivalent origins; thus the result is stable. Forcedness gives P⊆θ and leastness of θ among stable equivalences gives θ⊆P. At most E representatives are deleted and queued. Smaller-to-larger wire relabeling costs O(W log W). Deterministic split/join tree melding costs O(m log(n/m+1)); charging surviving entries to multiplicative map growth and deleted entries once gives O(E log(E+1)). Bounded-key initialization is O(W+E+B), and all retained structures are linear-space.
claims.witness: The independent checker compared a literal representative-map implementation with naive least closure on all 4 one-wire/two-box graphs, all 256 two-wire/two-box graphs, all 512 three-wire/one-box graphs, and 8,192 reproducibly selected cyclic three-wire/two-box graphs; every partition agreed and every pending count was at most E.
claims.search_method: Invariant proof, amortized tree-meld accounting, and finite comparison against naive closure on general directed instances.

claims.claim: Both outcomes have certificates of size O(W+E) verifiable deterministically in O(W+E+B) time.
claims.evidence: For a negative certificate, equality of supplied bounded labels is an equivalence. Sorting edges by (X,P(t)) and requiring one P(o) per group checks stability in linear bounded-key time. Since θ is contained in every stable equivalence, separation in P is sound; θ itself proves completeness. For a positive certificate, process chronological binary merge nodes inductively. Previously certified child subtrees are internally θ-equivalent, and the earlier q-subtree proves the cited targets equivalent, so the same-box edges force the two child components together. Distinct current roots, unique parent links, earlier-child indices, and unique wire leaves establish a forest. DFS intervals then verify every endpoint-containment citation in O(1), after O(W) preprocessing. Recording only class-changing forced merges gives at most W−1 internal nodes and proves completeness.
claims.witness: The first positive merge may cite a target-wire leaf as q; every later class-changing collision cites the existing merge-tree node containing both targets. A negative instance uses its actual θ class numbers.
claims.search_method: Soundness and completeness proofs for both certificate formats, including chronology, forest structure, stability, bounded-key sorting, and verifier accounting.

claims.claim: The target O(W+E+B) bound holds for graded dual graphs: graphs admitting an integer rank ρ with ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 for every edge (o,X,t).
claims.evidence: Identity classes are rank-homogeneous, and every fold maps equivalent rank-(r−1) targets to rank-r origins, so θ never crosses ranks. Consequently rank-r closure depends only on finalized rank-(r−1) classes and is exactly the connected-component closure of groups keyed by (X,class(t)). The total number of star edges is at most E. The equations ρ(o)−ρ(t)=1 can be assigned and checked by DFS in every weak component. A consistent component has potential span at most W−1 along a simple path, so componentwise normalization permits O(W)-sized buckets. Sparse grouping, recognition, and component searches therefore use O(W+E+B) time and space.
claims.witness: Across all forward two-box graphs on up to four ordered wires, the checker found 1, 4, 37, and 748 rank-consistent cases respectively; the rank sweep matched naive θ on every case.
claims.search_method: Rank-induction proof, difference-constraint recognition analysis, and exhaustive finite comparison on all ordered graphs through W=4.

claims.claim: Canonical longest-path box stratification is recognizable in O(W+E+B) time and includes non-graded instances with nontrivial folds.
claims.evidence: Topological sorting and dynamic programming compute longest-path levels in O(W+E); a cycle rejects the condition. Bucketing arcs by tail level and using a timestamped B-entry array checks the unique head-level condition in O(W+E+B), without a level-by-box table. In the stated witness, λ(a,b,c,d,e)=(0,1,1,2,2). The two X-arcs share tail a and force d≡e. Unit-difference grading is impossible because a→b→d forces ρ(d)−ρ(a)=2 while a→d forces it to equal 1. Assigning globally distinct pins realizes the arcs as a valid dual maze.
claims.witness: Feature arcs a→P b, b→Q d, a→R c, c→S e, a→X d, and a→X e form an accepted five-wire DAG with a nontrivial d≡e fold but no unit-difference rank.
claims.search_method: Direct recognition analysis and exact evaluation of the supplied strict non-graded witness.

claims.claim: In a box-stratified feature DAG, every class of the least folding equivalence θ is homogeneous in canonical level λ.
claims.evidence: Start with homogeneous singleton classes. If equivalent tails of same-box arcs have level s, stratification puts both heads at the same level. Adding that forced equality and taking equivalence closure therefore preserves homogeneity. Because the finite least closure can be generated by at most W−1 class-changing folds, induction proves the invariant for θ. Every feature arc strictly increases longest-path level, so a level-r origin depends only on strictly lower levels; it need not be exactly level r−1.
claims.witness: The checker tested level homogeneity on every accepted two-box ordered DAG through W=4—1, 4, 43, and 913 accepted instances—and found no cross-level θ class.
claims.search_method: Induction over generated folds plus exhaustive enumeration of all accepted ordered two-box DAGs through four wires.

claims.claim: A level-by-level star decomposition computes θ, and hence exit reachability, in O(W+E+B) time and space on box-stratified feature DAGs.
claims.evidence: Inductively, all classes strictly below r are final when level r is processed. Grouping level-r heads by (X,class(t)) therefore adds only θ-forced star edges, proving P⊆θ. Conversely, if same-box arcs have P-equivalent tails, P's level homogeneity gives a common tail level s; stratification gives their heads a common level r>s. Their target class was final when r was processed, so those heads were joined in the same star group. Thus P is stable, and leastness gives θ⊆P. Nested sparse grouping can use timestamp arrays indexed separately by boxes and class identifiers. Each group contributes at most one fewer star edge than input arcs, allowing ordinary linear-time component searches.
claims.witness: The level sweep exactly matched naive least folding closure on all 913 accepted four-wire/two-box ordered DAGs, as well as every accepted instance for W<4.
claims.search_method: Proof of both partition inclusions, implementation accounting, and exhaustive comparison on the complete ordered W≤4 test universe.

claims.claim: Repeated global fixed-point rescanning can require Θ(W) changing rounds even with one box and E=Θ(W).
claims.evidence: Initially only the equal-target pair at level zero fires. If exactly pairs a_j≡b_j for j<k have been obtained, then the level-k edge targets become equivalent while every higher pair still has inequivalent targets; thus changing round k+1 adds exactly a_k≡b_k. Different levels and z never merge. This yields n+1 changing rounds for W=2n+3 and E=2n+2. Conversely every changing round reduces the number of classes, so no instance has more than W−1 such rounds. Distinct pins, plus an unused outer pin if needed, realize the family with one recursive box.
claims.witness: Exact simulation for every n from 0 through 16 returned (W,E,rounds)=(2n+3,2n+2,n+1), ending at (35,32,17).
claims.search_method: Induction on synchronous rounds, universal class-count upper bound, and exact simulation of seventeen family members.

claims.claim: Any folding implementation that explicitly stores every live box representative per class and handles each class union by scanning all representatives of one operand has an Ω((W+E+B) log(W+E+B)) worst case.
claims.evidence: The construction can be made explicit with N−1 fresh boxes serializing the balanced data merge tree, N anchor-rule boxes, N boxes Y_i, and one final query box. It has W=4N+2, E=6N, and B=3N. Before anchors enter the root, a data class containing k data wires has k distinct live Y-keys. At merge-tree level k there are N/2^(k+1) unions whose two operands each contain 2^k such keys. Scanning either operand therefore costs at least 2^k, totaling N/2 per level and Ω(N log N) over log₂N levels. The dependency boxes leave exactly one class-changing fold enabled at each step, so scheduling cannot avoid these balanced unions. Removing either occurrence of any Y_i breaks the eventual start-to-outer equality, confirming that these keys are query-relevant.
claims.witness: For N=2,4,8,16,32, the checker reconstructed the exact W/E/B counts, verified a unique enabled class-changing fold throughout, and verified both occurrences of every Y_i were load-bearing. At N=32 it obtained (W,E,B)=(130,192,96) and 160 mandatory representative inspections during the balanced phase, exceeding the symbolic floor N log₂N/2=80.
claims.search_method: Explicit reconstruction of the serialized family, per-level counting proof under the stated eager-scanning model, and exact checks through N=32.

claims.claim: The bounded-key radix sorts used above rely only on the standard lexicographic stable-pass invariant, not on preservation of earlier-key blocks.
claims.evidence: After a stable sort on the secondary key b, a stable sort on primary key a orders the a-values and preserves nondecreasing b-order within every equal-a group. Preservation of global b-blocks is neither true nor required. The relevant coordinate ranges are bounded by W and B, so the two counting-sort passes take O(W+E+B) time and space.
claims.witness: The checker sorted records containing repeated full keys and obtained exact lexicographic order while retaining original order within the repeated (2,1) key.
claims.search_method: Direct stable-sort invariant proof and an exact repeated-key test.

target_evidence: The source asks for an unrestricted deterministic O(W+E+B)-time exit-reachability algorithm in the source representation. The draft does not establish that entire target: its unrestricted sparse-map algorithm retains a logarithmic factor, linear certificate verification does not find certificates in linear time, and its source-linear constructors require graded or box-stratified structure. Those results are nevertheless correct material progress, particularly the deterministic sparse general algorithm, linear certificates, and recognizable linear-time subclasses. The draft explicitly labels its resolution PARTIAL and states that the unrestricted target remains open, so its claimed resolution is accurate.
